traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Myrtaceae (read 2026-10-17): lamina entire; German Wikipedia, Myrtengewächse (read 2026-10-17): blade simple and entire-margined.

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 347: stamens many, centripetal, free or joined in 4-5 groups (Floral Diagrams p. 212: 4 to many). Book writes ∞ (numerous); 200 is our stand-in for the upper bound and 20 for 'numerous' with no stated lower bound.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 347: carpels 2 to 5, up to 16.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 347: 4 to 5 petals, perianth parts free or (Eucalyptus) joined into a lid. Free petals: rotate by PlantGen's free-petal rule; the book names no other corolla form. Petals fall early (Floral Diagrams p. 212).

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 162 Myrtaceae: trees or shrubs; leaves simple, mostly entire, opposite or rarely alternate (eucalypts' adult leaves alternate), dotted with oil glands; no stipules, or tiny ones; flowers mostly regular; calyx tube joined to the ovary; petals 4 or 5; stamens numerous, rarely few, on the rim of the disc lining the calyx tube (read as a hypanthium); ovary inferior; fruit splitting along its cells or staying shut (capsules in eucalypts and bottlebrushes, berries in myrtles and guavas).

traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Myrtaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Heteropyxidaceae, Psiloxylaceae: how long the leaves last (character 37), coded usually evergreen, rarely deciduous. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 347, 348, family Myrtaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite (dioecious in Psiloxylon), usually. Read together as {"hermaphrodite": "usually", "dioecious": "rarely"}.
